correctness.rationale: For a side-preserving finite G-action on any nonempty complete K_(R,C), a geometrically fixed point of the matching simplicial realization has barycentric coefficients constant on each edge orbit. It is supported on invariant matchings precisely when each selected edge orbit is itself pairwise disjoint. The first/second projections of an eligible edge orbit to its transitive row and column G-orbits are both injective and surjective, hence it is the graph of a G-equivariant bijection. Such maps exist only between isomorphic stabilizer types G/H, with exactly |N_G(H)/H| choices per orbit pair. Two distinct eligible orbits coexist iff they use distinct row and column G-orbit indices; this is precisely the face rule of a matching complex of w_H K_(a_H,b_H), and disjoint stabilizer types form their simplicial join. The orbit-barycenter map is a PL homeomorphism (not just a bijection of invariant vertices). In the five-regular-orbit case w=|G|; forgetting/choosing a parallel-edge color gives simplicial section/retraction to M(K_5,5), so known H~2=Z/3 is a direct summand, not merely torsion of unspecified order. The 2-by-2 weighted block decomposes into two K_(w,w) graph components, cycle rank (w-1)^2. The proof holds for every finite group, with empty geometric fixed locus when no eligible edge orbit exists; finite code enumerations remain checks only.

value.rationale: This is a complete classification of a natural geometric fixed-point construction for arbitrary finite G-set actions, detecting the stabilizer type and Weyl-normalizer multiplicity. It connects equivariant orbit data with concrete chessboard homology and demonstrates that fixed spaces can have split 3-torsion for every nontrivial finite group. Not a routine fixed-vertex count: geometric barycenters and simultaneous shore orbits are essential.

limitations: Shore-preserving action on complete bipartite graph, finite G, nonempty shores. Does not classify shore swaps, missing edges, residual normalizer action, or full homology of wK_(5,5).
